                    ### Question
                    A 37-year-old man presents a picture of arthritis of the metacarpophalangeal of both hands and a right pleuritis. On examination, bilateral malar erythema was observed. Positive antinuclear antibodies are detected (titre 1/640), with native anti-DNA antibodies also positive; Anti-Sm negative. What would be the initial treatment of choice for this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Glucocorticoids at high doses.
opb. Glucocorticoids and mycophenolate.
opc. Non-steroidal and antimalarial anti-inflammatories.
opd. The picture will probably be self-limiting and does not require treatment.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient presents with symptoms consistent with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), including arthritis, pleuritis, and bilateral malar erythema, alongside positive antinuclear antibodies and anti-DNA antibodies, indicating significant disease activity. The standard initial treatment for active SLE, particularly with severe manifestations, is glucocorticoids, often at high doses to control inflammation and prevent further complications. This aligns with the consensus that glucocorticoids are first-line therapy in such cases. Other options, such as non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs or antimalarials, may be considered for milder cases or as adjunctive therapy but are not the initial treatment of choice for severe disease.
